questions.q: How long does this lesson's recommended walkthrough structure target?
options: About 30 seconds
There's no time guidance -- length doesn't matter
Roughly 5-10 minutes, across five parts
A full hour, covering every field built
questions.explain: The five-part structure is built to fit a typical portfolio review or interview slot, roughly ten minutes total.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend telling ONE automation story in depth, rather than summarizing all three (the Flow, a validation rule, the approval process)?
options: Only one piece of automation was actually finished
Time limits make it technically impossible to describe more than one automation item
An interviewer remembers one well-told problem/decision/build/result story better than three rushed summaries, and the other two stay ready for follow-up questions
Validation rules and approval processes aren't worth mentioning in an interview
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames this as a memorability choice -- depth on one story beats breadth across three rushed ones.

questions.q: According to this lesson, where does the answer to "why is OWD Private instead of Public Read Only" come from?
options: Lesson 4's security design -- deal values and installer data are sensitive by default
Lesson 9's custom object field list
Lesson 15's report folder structure
Lesson 16's sample data loading order
questions.explain: The security-model design reasoning from Lesson 4 is the source for this answer, since it explains why Private was chosen as the baseline for every core object.

questions.q: What does this lesson suggest bringing as a visual aid during the walkthrough, beyond just talking through the build?
options: The Lesson 3 data model diagram and the Lesson 11 role hierarchy, or a short screen recording of the dashboard and a Flow running
A printed copy of every validation rule's Apex code
Nothing -- visuals are discouraged in a portfolio review
A spreadsheet listing every user ever created in the org
questions.explain: The lesson recommends the data model diagram, the role hierarchy, and (for recorded presentations) a short screen recording, since a reviewer following a picture retains more than words alone.

questions.q: Where does this lesson say the honest answer to "what would you build next" should come from?
options: Lesson 1's Definition of Done
Lesson 18's Known Limitations section
The Lesson 15 report folder list
It should be improvised on the spot with no preparation
questions.explain: Lesson 18's Known Limitations section already lists what the build deliberately left out, making it the direct source for an honest, prepared answer about next steps.
